warmup/why: The learning rate does not have to stay fixed. Big steps make fast progress early on, and small steps settle in at the end.
warmup/ramp: Many runs begin with a warmup: the rate climbs in a straight line from zero to its peak over the first k steps.
warmup/ex: With a peak of zero point one over a thousand steps, step two hundred and fifty runs at a quarter of the peak: zero point zero two five.
warmup/reason: Why bother? At the start, far from any minimum, the gradients are at their largest and least steady. A full-size step on them can overshoot and blow up, so warmup eases in.
steps/rule: The classic decay goes in steps: multiply the rate by a factor, often zero point one, every so many steps.
steps/ex: Start at zero point one and drop every ten thousand steps: step fifteen thousand runs at zero point zero one, and step twenty-five thousand at zero point zero zero one.
cosine/cos: Cosine decay glides down instead, along half a cosine wave, from eta max to eta min over T steps.
cosine/shape: It starts flat, falls fastest in the middle, and flattens out again at the end.
cosine/half: Halfway through, the cosine is zero, so the rate sits halfway between. From zero point one down to zero, that is zero point zero five.
cosine/third: A third of the way in, the cosine of pi over three is a half, so the rate is three quarters of the peak: zero point zero seven five.
